mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) relative to its historical average is associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns, as lower rates reduce the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows.
failure_condition: Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% over the past month predicts positive 5-day S&P 500 returns, as a tight labor market supports consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.0% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect between HOUST and RSAFS has a Rank IC below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (INDPRO growth > 1.0% YoY), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past month predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 returns, as it signals weakening economic momentum.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO growth > 1.0% YoY, the Rank IC between INDPRO change and 60-day SPX returns is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) is associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 returns, as strong housing activity signals robust consumer demand and economic growth.
failure_condition: Rank IC between HOUST and 20-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 3.5% year-over-year predicts negative 5-day S&P 500 returns, as higher inflation pressures the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which drives positive 60-day S&P 500 returns by supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The interaction effect between PAYEMS and UNRATE has a Rank IC below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In an early-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 growth > 1.5% YoY), a rise in GDP growth predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns, as economic recovery boosts corporate profits.
failure_condition: In periods where GDPC1 growth > 1.5% YoY, the Rank IC between GDPC1 growth and 20-day SPX returns is less than 0.03.
